title: Reproduction
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.6.1-c33 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c15 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c18 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.6.1-q07, 4.6.1-q10, 4.6.1-q08, 4.6.1-q11, 4.6.1-q09, 4.6.1-q12, 4.6.1-q13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Genotype
items.clue: The alleles present in an organism.

items.label: Gene
items.clue: A small section of DNA on a chromosome.

items.label: Nucleotide
items.clue: The repeating unit from which the DNA polymer is made.

items.label: Meiosis
items.clue: The type of cell division that leads to non-identical cells being formed.

questions.stem: A grower has one healthy strawberry plant and wants many identical plants quickly. Why is reproduction by runners an advantage here?

options.text: Two parents share the work, so less time and energy are needed here.
One parent is needed and it is faster than sexual reproduction.
The offspring produced will show useful variation from the parent.
The plant can use only one method, so it cannot produce any seeds.

questions.explanation: Advantages of asexual reproduction are that only one parent is needed, it is faster than sexual reproduction, and many identical offspring can be produced when conditions are favourable.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the structure of DNA?

options.text: A chemical stored loosely in the cell's cytoplasm
A polymer of four bases joined into two long strands
A polymer of amino acids joined in one long chain
A polymer of two strands forming a double helix

questions.explanation: DNA is a polymer made up of two strands forming a double helix, contained in structures called chromosomes.

questions.stem: Which statement about organisms that reproduce by both methods is correct?

options.text: Daffodils reproduce by bulb division, fusing gametes.
Malarial parasites reproduce only by one method, asexually.
Fungi reproduce asexually by spores to give variation.
Malarial parasites reproduce sexually in the mosquito.

questions.explanation: Malarial parasites reproduce asexually in the human host, but sexually in the mosquito.

questions.stem: What is meant by the genome of an organism?

options.text: The amino acids that make up an organism's DNA
The parts of the DNA that code for proteins
The genetic material found in the cytoplasm
The entire genetic material of an organism

questions.explanation: The genome of an organism is the entire genetic material of that organism.

questions.stem: A population of fungi lives in a habitat where conditions are beginning to change. Why may reproducing sexually be an advantage?

options.text: Asexual reproduction is what produces the variation needed in this habitat.
It is faster and uses less energy than reproducing asexually would be.
It produces variation, giving a survival advantage by natural selection.
Fungi can use only one method, so they have to reproduce sexually here.

questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction produces variation in the offspring, and if the environment changes variation gives a survival advantage by natural selection.

questions.stem: A gene in a mouse is linked to brown fur. What does that gene code for?

options.text: The brown fur characteristic directly
A certain sequence of amino acids
One amino acid for each single base
An entire chromosome in the nucleus

questions.explanation: Each gene codes for a particular sequence of amino acids, to make a specific protein.

questions.stem: Which of these is one of the uses of understanding the human genome?

options.text: Finding the gene that directly builds a feature
Removing non-coding DNA, which has no effect
Searching for genes linked to some diseases
Listing all genes that code for a protein

questions.explanation: Understanding the human genome is important for the search for genes linked to different types of disease, the understanding and treatment of inherited disorders, and tracing human migration patterns from the past.
